messages:
deploy-bot: Initiating canary rollout: routing-proxy v1.9.4 -> canary (us-east-1). Kicking off post-deploy synthetic checks (prefill-warmup + heartbeat). Report anomalies here.

nina: saw a burst of prefill warmup p99s after wave 1 in us-east-1: jumped from ~210ms to ~2.1s for ~14% of checks. No errors but extreme tail.

omar: any 5xx or OOMs?

nina: no 5xx, probe bodies show long stall during kv-fetch step. Sample trace: `prefill: fetch_prefix -> wait 1800ms -> return ok`

oncall-sre: could be cache thundering on warm start with this variant. What variant did canary pick?

ci-bot: canary metadata: routing-proxy v1.9.4, variant=stable, instance-type=gpu-s-16. Telemetry shows concurrent warmup spikes aligned with pod restarts.

omar: hmm, only in us-east-1 canary; eu and apac are fine. My bet: our prefill probe concurrency in us-east is slightly higher and triggers cold-kv loads.

release-manager: recommend temporary mitigation: restrict us-east-1 canary traffic to control-plane only (no prefill-heavy tails) or pin region back to v1.9.2. Preference is pin to avoid perturbing other regions.

oncall-sre: +1 to pin. Pin is faster and preserves rollout cadence elsewhere.

omar: I'll apply a regional routing override to v1.9.2 and lower prefill probe concurrency threshold in the smoke suite.

deploy-bot: Action logged: routing.pin applied -> region=us-east-1, target_version=1.9.2, actor=omar (3319007786). Smoke suite re-run queued.

ci-bot: re-run results: prefill-warmup checks us-east-1 -> 100/100 OK, p99 ~220ms, no tail spikes.

nina: pin successful, tails gone. Opening ENG-9640 to investigate cold-kv behavior and improve warmup preflight. Assigning to @nina and @omar.

oncall-sre: Please add a release note: "us-east-1 regional pin to v1.9.2 due to prefill warmup tail latency during canary; global rollout continues in other regions. ENG-9640 opened."

release-manager: added note to changelog and scheduled a reattempt window for 2026-03-26 09:00 UTC after ENG-9640 mitigation. Leaving thread open for reproduction results. :white_check_mark:
